question.title: Average Order Value by Customer
question.desc: Find the average order value for each customer, considering only orders placed in 2022. The average order value should be calculated as the total order value divided by the number of orders. Sort the results by customer name.
question.setup: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS customers; CREATE TABLE customers (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100)); INSERT INTO customers (name) VALUES ('John Doe'), ('Jane Doe'), ('Bob Smith'); DROP TABLE IF EXISTS orders; CREATE TABLE orders (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, order_date DATE, total DECIMAL(10, 2), FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id)); INSERT INTO orders (customer_id, order_date, total) VALUES (1, '2022-01-01', 100.00), (1, '2022-01-15', 200.00), (2, '2022-02-01', 50.00), (3, '2022-03-01', 150.00), (1, '2021-01-01', 120.00);
question.solution: WITH customer_orders AS (SELECT c.name, o.total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2022) SELECT name, AVG(total) AS average_order_value FROM customer_orders GROUP BY name ORDER BY name;
question.tips: Consider using window functions for more complex aggregations.
hints: Start by filtering orders to only those in 2022.
Use a JOIN to connect customers with their orders.
Apply the AVG aggregation function to calculate the average order value per customer.
